other.label: CBO cost estimate: S. 1533, a bill to amend title 38, United States Code, to make permanent and codify the pilot program for use of contract physicians for disability examinations, and for other purposes

summary: This bill makes permanent and codifies the existing pilot program that allows the Department of Veterans Affairs to use contract physicians, rather than only Department employees, to conduct medical disability examinations for benefit applicants. It sets rules for health care professional licensure across state lines, specifies the source of funds for these exams, requires a mechanism to transmit new medical evidence, terminates the previous pilot program, and mandates a report to Congress within three years.

affected_groups.effect: May have their medical disability examinations conducted by contract physicians instead of Department employees.
affected_groups.group: Applicants for Department of Veterans Affairs benefits

affected_groups.effect: Can conduct disability examinations pursuant to a contract at any location in any state if they meet specific licensure requirements and are within their authorized duties.

key_provisions: Authorizes the Under Secretary for Benefits to contract with persons other than Department employees to perform medical disability examinations.
Allows qualified contract health care professionals with a current unrestricted license in any state to conduct examinations at any location in any state, regardless of other state licensure laws.
Directs that expenses for carrying out these examinations be reimbursed from amounts available to the Secretary for the payment of compensation and pensions.
Requires the Secretary to establish a mechanism for contract health care professionals to transmit new and material medical evidence introduced during exams back to the Secretary.
Terminates the previous pilot program for the use of contract physicians for disability examinations.
Requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to submit a report to Congress within three years on the effect of this authority on the cost, timeliness, and thoroughness of exams.

summary_detail.plain_summary: This bill makes permanent and codifies the existing pilot program that allows the Department of Veterans Affairs to use contract physicians, rather than only Department employees, to conduct medical disability examinations for benefit applicants. It sets rules for health care professional licensure across state lines, specifies the source of funds for these exams, requires a mechanism to transmit new medical evidence, terminates the previous pilot program, and mandates a report to Congress within three years.
summary_detail.significance: This bill permanently establishes the use of contract physicians for veterans' disability exams and sets uniform interstate licensure rules for those physicians. Because the source text does not specify the exact number of individuals affected or the total monetary costs, the significance is assessed as moderate.
